deep.reconstruction:
The page is a short memo of two indefinite integrals. They are the working formulas behind the evaluation on the previous page, where the double integral Ω = ∫_0^∞∫_0^∞ (cos ax − cos bx) e^{−tx} dt dx is computed in both orders to evaluate ω = ∫_0^∞ (cos ax − cos bx)/x dx.

(1) ∫ e^{−tx} cos(ax) dx = (a sin ax − t cos ax)/(t² + a²) · e^{−tx}.

(2) ∫ e^{−tx} sin(ax) dx = (−a cos ax − t sin ax)/(t² + a²) · e^{−tx}.

The previous page says these are 'easily confirmed by differentiation'. Here is that check (my filling-in).
- For (1): d/dx[(a sin ax − t cos ax) e^{−tx}] = e^{−tx}[a² cos ax + a t sin ax − t a sin ax + t² cos ax] = (a² + t²) e^{−tx} cos ax.
- For (2): d/dx[(−a cos ax − t sin ax) e^{−tx}] = e^{−tx}[a² sin ax − a t cos ax + a t cos ax + t² sin ax] = (a² + t²) e^{−tx} sin ax.

Taking limits x = 0 to ∞ (t > 0) gives the Laplace transforms used in the double-integral argument:
- ∫_0^∞ e^{−tx} cos ax dx = t/(t² + a²).
- ∫_0^∞ e^{−tx} sin ax dx = a/(t² + a²).

The cosine formula yields, as on the previous page:
- ∫_0^∞ (cos ax − cos bx) e^{−tx} dx = t/(a² + t²) − t/(b² + t²).
- Integrating in t gives Ω = ½ log(b²/a²), hence ω = log(b/a) (written for a, b of the same sign; in general it is log|b/a|).

The sine formula is not used on the surviving pages. Plausibly (my conjecture) it was recorded for the companion evaluation ∫_0^∞ sin(ax)/x dx = ∫_0^∞ a/(a² + t²) dt = (π/2)·sgn(a), by the same interchange of integrations.
errors: No errors on this page; both antiderivatives are correct.
Minor point in context: Gauss interchanges the order of integration in the conditionally convergent double integral without justification. This was standard practice for the period.
